sheet-1.description: This part of the first sheet of the 1924 New Egypt atlas shows North New Egypt, the thinly built settlement on the road north of the village, drawn at 50 feet to an inch around the key map and index that fill the upper right of the sheet. Main runs up the left-centre of the sheet from the bottom edge, crosses a creek on a wooden bridge and continues north as an unpaved road drawn with dashed lines; a second dashed road branches west from it north of the creek. Compton leaves Main eastwards in the lower half of the sheet and runs to the right edge. The area is largely open land, marked vacant beyond on every side, with scattered frame dwellings, stables, hen houses and storage sheds on large lots. Named buildings include the Glenside House and Lakeview House, both summer boarding houses, north of the creek, and the Prospect House, another summer boarding house, in the lower left corner. A basket factory and an old brick-filled building stand on Compton. Block numbers 13 to 16 are printed across the area. The creek flows west across the middle of the sheet from a small pond near the dividing line. The heavy line that encloses the key map and street index marks the limit of this part; the key map at 700 feet to an inch, the water facilities and fire department notes and the location map of New Jersey are outside it and not georeferenced. A compass rose stands at the left edge.
notes: Main north of the village is today's North Main Street; Compton is Brown Lane.
The dashed road branching west north of the creek is probably today's Bright Road; its junction is drawn only with dashed lines and was not used as control.
Placed from the Main / Compton junction alone, with the atlas scale and a north direction from the compass and the dashed-road junction: low confidence.

map. Key map (700 ft to an inch, not georeferenced), index, water and fire notes, and North New Egypt at 50 ft: Main (North Main Street) with Compton (Brown Lane) and a dashed road west of Main north of the creek (probably Bright Road). Mask cuts out the key map and index box (heavy line). Placed from one junction (Main / Compton) with the atlas scale and north from the dashed-road junction and the compass: low confidence.

sheet-2-1.description: The lower and larger part of sheet 2 shows Main, today's North Main Street, running north-east from its junction with Fort Avenue and Lakewood Avenue, at 50 feet to an inch and drawn at a different angle from the upper part of the sheet. Lakewood Avenue, also lettered Goshen, leaves the junction eastward along the bottom of the part, and Fort Avenue enters from the lower left. The area is residential: frame dwellings with stables, sheds and auto houses along both sides of Main and the north side of Lakewood Avenue, and a few dwellings on the south side of Lakewood Avenue at the bottom edge. Long, irregular lots run back from Main to open land marked vacant beyond on the east. Block numbers 12, 13 and 14 are printed in the blocks, and a building with a brick part stands at the left edge near the junction. A water pipe runs in Main and Lakewood Avenue. A compass rose stands in the open land to the right of Main. The upper edge of the part, along the heavy dividing line, is marked no exposure; the blocks beyond it are drawn on the upper part of the sheet and on sheet 3, whose number is printed at the lower left.
notes: Main here is today's North Main Street; Lakewood Avenue (Goshen) is Lakewood Road.
Placed from the Main / Lakewood Avenue junction alone, with the atlas scale and north from the direction of Main: low confidence.

map, 50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line at different rotations: part 1 (lower) Main (North Main Street) north-east of Fort Av and Lakewood Av (Goshen) (Lakewood Road); part 2 (upper) Fort Av between Railroad Av (Evergreen Road) and Main, M. E. Church, Public School, Pond.

sheet-2-2.description: The upper part of sheet 2 shows Fort Avenue running east from Railroad Avenue to Main, north of the village centre, at 50 feet to an inch. Railroad Avenue, today's Evergreen Road, runs down the left edge of the part; a creek and a pond fill the upper left corner between Railroad Avenue and the first lots. Main, today's North Main Street, crosses the right edge with the start of Lakewood Avenue (Goshen) lettered beside it. The north side of Fort Avenue holds the Public School, a frame building in the middle of the block, the M. E. Church with its parsonage, horse sheds and outbuildings near Main, and a row of frame dwellings with auto houses and a coop. The south side has dwellings, a wagon shed and storage near Railroad Avenue and is otherwise open, with lots running back to the heavy line marked no exposure that divides the sheet; the blocks beyond are on sheet 3. A small office and a hose house stand on Railroad Avenue at the lower left. Water pipes run in Railroad Avenue and Main, and a north arrow is drawn in the block north of Fort Avenue. Block numbers 2, 7, 8 and 13 are printed.
notes: Railroad Avenue is today's Evergreen Road; Main is North Main Street; Lakewood Avenue (Goshen) is Lakewood Road.
Placed by a helmert fit through two junctions along Fort Avenue: low to medium confidence.

map, 50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line at different rotations: part 1 (lower) Main (North Main Street) north-east of Fort Av and Lakewood Av (Goshen) (Lakewood Road); part 2 (upper) Fort Av between Railroad Av (Evergreen Road) and Main, M. E. Church, Public School, Pond.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 covers the east side of the village centre at 50 feet to an inch. Main runs across the sheet from Railroad Avenue at the left edge to Church, where it turns north-east and continues to the top right corner; today the turn is the junction of Main Street and North Main Street. Church (also lettered Front) runs south from Main to Front Street, which is lettered Front (Church) to the west and Front Street or Magnolia Avenue to the east. The block between Main and Front holds the commercial centre: stores, the American House hotel, a moving picture theatre of concrete block, a garage for twenty cars, a tin shop and stove store, and a hall. The Presbyterian Church stands on the south side of Front. North of Main a small brook crosses meadow land from the left, past a livery stable, a garage and dwellings, to the north-east part of the sheet, where the Colonial House and The Cedarbrook stand among large dwellings on Main. The south-east part of the sheet is thinly built, with dwellings along Front Street or Magnolia Avenue and open land marked vacant beyond at the bottom. Water pipes run in all the streets, and a compass rose is drawn in the upper left. Block numbers 3, 4, 5 and 11 are printed.
notes: Railroad Avenue is today's Evergreen Road; Main north-east of Church is North Main Street; Church (Front) is Church Street; Front Street or Magnolia Avenue is Magnolia Avenue east of Church Street and Front Street to the west.
Placed from three junctions (an exact fit): medium confidence.

map, 50 ft. Main between Railroad Av (Evergreen Road) and Church (Front) (Church Street), Main north-east of Church (North Main Street), Front (Church) and Front St or Magnolia Av (Front Street / Magnolia Avenue). Movies, American House, Presbyterian Church, Colonial House, The Cedarbrook.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 covers the west side of the village centre at 50 feet to an inch, where Main crosses Crosswicks Creek on an iron bridge below the dam of Oakford Lake. East of the creek, Main is lined with the post office, a bank, stores, a printing office, wagon sheds and the fire house; Railroad Avenue runs north from Main at the upper right, and Mill runs south to Front (Church) and beyond. West of the creek, Oakford Avenue runs south from Main past S. Liebovitz and Sons' shirt factory and M. E. Lamb's feed mill on the head race, then turns west along the lower part of the sheet. Between Oakford Avenue and the left edge stand the Town Hall, G. Halpin's wagon shop and auto repairing shop, and the plant of the New Egypt Light, Heat, Power and Water Co., with its engines, a flowing well and a reservoir. North of Main, the Oakford Lake House and its outbuildings occupy a large lot. The creek, the head race and Oakford Lake fill the middle of the lower half of the sheet, with a dam and gate. Dwellings with stables and sheds fill the remaining lots. Water pipes run in Main, Oakford Avenue and Mill. A compass rose is drawn in the upper left, and block numbers 1, 2, 4, 5 and 17 are printed.
notes: Railroad Avenue is today's Evergreen Road; Mill is Brindletown Road; Front (Church) is Front Street; the north-south leg of Oakford Avenue is today's Lakeview Drive.
Iron bridge over Crosswicks Creek on Main; dam and gate at the head of Oakford Lake.

map, 50 ft. Main across Crosswicks Creek (iron bridge), Oakford Av (north-south leg now Lakeview Drive), Mill (Brindletown Road), Railroad Av (Evergreen Road), Front (Church); Oakford Lake, light and water company, feed mill, shirt factory.

sheet-5-1.description: The lower and larger part of sheet 5 shows the west end of the village at 50 feet to an inch, drawn at a different angle from the upper part of the sheet. Main enters from the right and meets Jacobstown Road and Maple Avenue at the upper right of the part. Maple Avenue runs west across the part to the left edge; Chestnut, also lettered Charlevoix, runs south from Maple Avenue to Oakford Avenue, which crosses the lower part of the sheet. The area is residential: frame dwellings with auto houses, stables and sheds on narrow lots facing Maple Avenue, Oakford Avenue and Main, a blacksmith shop on the south side of Maple Avenue, and a dwelling of concrete block on Oakford Avenue. A garage stands at the corner of Main and Jacobstown Road. A water tank of 42,000 gallons on a steel tower stands in the block west of Chestnut. Open land marked vacant beyond lies along the bottom and the left edge, which is marked no exposure. A creek crosses under Jacobstown Road at the top of the part. Water pipes run in Maple Avenue, Oakford Avenue and Main, and a north arrow is drawn at the upper right. Block numbers 10, 17, 18 and 19 are printed.
notes: Chestnut (Charlevoix) is today's Chestnut Street.
Placed from three junctions (an exact fit): medium confidence.

map, 50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line at different rotations: part 1 (lower) Maple Av, Chestnut (Charlevoix), Oakford Av, Main and Jacobstown Rd; part 2 (upper) Jacobstown Rd west of the creek with the P. & A. R.R. (U. T. Co. lessee), milk depot and Ward Harker saw mill.

sheet-5-2.description: The upper part of sheet 5 shows Jacobstown Road west of the village and the railroad, at 50 feet to an inch and at a different angle from the lower part. Jacobstown Road runs along the top of the part from the left edge to the upper right, with a row of frame dwellings, stables and coops on long lots on its south side and a few buildings on the north side. The Pennsylvania and Atlantic Railroad (Union Transportation Co., lessee) crosses Jacobstown Road at the right and runs south-west across the part with a siding. Beside the track at the bottom of the part stand the Supplee-Wills-Jones Milk Co. milk depot with its platform, and a lumber shed, storage building, coal shed and office of a lumber and coal yard. Ward Harker's saw mill, not in operation, stands at the left. A creek crosses the lower right corner. Most of the area is open land marked vacant beyond, and the left edge is marked vacant. A compass rose is drawn at the left. Block numbers 2 and 10 are printed. The heavy line along the bottom of the part separates it from the lower part of the sheet.
notes: The railroad (P. and A. R.R., U. T. Co. lessee) is abandoned; its line in OpenStreetMap is TIGER-derived.
Placed from the Jacobstown Road / railroad crossing alone, with the atlas scale and north from the direction of Jacobstown Road: low confidence.

map, 50 ft. Two parts split by a heavy line at different rotations: part 1 (lower) Maple Av, Chestnut (Charlevoix), Oakford Av, Main and Jacobstown Rd; part 2 (upper) Jacobstown Rd west of the creek with the P. & A. R.R. (U. T. Co. lessee), milk depot and Ward Harker saw mill.

sheet-6-1.description: The main part of sheet 6 shows Railroad Avenue north of the village and the railroad station, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the sheet turned so that north points about 48 degrees to the right. Railroad Avenue runs diagonally from the lower left, where it crosses the Pennsylvania and Atlantic Railroad (Union Transportation Co., lessee) beside the passenger station, to the upper right corner. Along it stand frame dwellings with stables and coops on long, narrow lots, horse sheds, and the Church of the Assumption (Roman Catholic). South of the track lie the freight depot, the Laurel Inn, a garage, warehouses for agricultural implements, hay and sand, Herman J. Morton's coal yard with coal bins and a trestle, and the car repairing shop of the Union Transportation Co. Crosswicks Creek runs down the left edge to a pond at the bottom. A water tank with a gasoline engine and pump stands by the track. A cow yard is drawn behind the dwellings on the east side of the avenue. Open land marked vacant beyond surrounds the built area. A compass rose stands at the lower right, beside the heavy lines that cut off the other two parts of the sheet.
notes: Railroad Avenue is today's Evergreen Road.

Placed from the Railroad Avenue / railroad crossing alone, with the atlas scale and north from the direction of Railroad Avenue; the abandoned railroad's line in OpenStreetMap is TIGER-derived: low confidence.

map, 50 ft. Three parts split by heavy lines: part 1 Railroad Av (Evergreen Road) north of the pond with the passenger station, freight depot and Union Transportation Co. shops (rotated about 48 degrees); part 2 (top left) Mill (Brindletown Road) south of Front; part 3 (bottom right) New Egypt Ice Co. on a private road by the railroad.

Not georeferenced on this sheet: New Egypt Ice Co. on a private road beside the P. & A. railroad (no street junction or surviving road; the railroad is abandoned and only a TIGER-derived line in OpenStreetMap; needs hand-picked parcel corners or the old rail right-of-way matched against parcels (step 6b)).

sheet-6-2.description: The upper left part of sheet 6 continues Mill south from sheet 4, at 50 feet to an inch and drawn with Mill running straight down the page. Mill, a street about 35 feet wide with a water pipe, has frame dwellings with stables and auto houses on the west side and a cabinet shop near the bottom; the east side has a few dwellings on long lots that run back to open land marked vacant beyond. The left edge of the part is marked no exposure, and the bottom edge, along the heavy line, is marked no exposure as well. A north arrow is drawn in the lots west of Mill. Block numbers 1 and 5 are printed, and the number 4 at the top refers to sheet 4.
notes: Mill is today's Brindletown Road.
No junction is drawn; placed from two lot corners carried from sheet 4 with the atlas scale and north from the direction of Mill: low confidence.
